Glossary and symbols

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-glossary.qmd

Every term and symbol medfit prints, in one place. Each links to the page that uses it. The formulas are the ones in Methods and Formulas, which also states the assumptions.

Variables and paths

Symbol Meaning
\(X\) the treatment
\(M\), \(M_1, \dots, M_K\) the mediator or mediators
\(Y\) the outcome
\(C\) covariates (the same set in every model unless stated)
\(a\) the path from treatment to mediator (a_path)
\(b\) the path from mediator to outcome, adjusting for the treatment (b_path)
\(c'\) the direct path from treatment to outcome, adjusting for the mediator (c_prime)
\(d\) a path from one mediator to the next in a chain (serial)
\(\theta_3\) the coefficient of the treatment-by-mediator product (interaction)

In the model \(M = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X + \gamma^\top C + e_M\) and \(Y = \theta_0 + \theta_1 X + \theta_2 M + \theta_4^\top C + e_Y\), the paths are \(a = \beta_1\), \(b = \theta_2\) and \(c' = \theta_1\).

Effects

Term Meaning Function
NIE natural indirect effect: the part of the effect that goes through the mediator; \(a b\) for one mediator nie()
NDE natural direct effect: the part that does not; \(c'\) for one mediator nde()
TE total effect: NIE + NDE te()
PM proportion mediated: NIE / TE pm()
chain effect the indirect effect through every mediator in a chain, \(a \, d_1 \cdots b\) nie() on a serial object
total indirect effect the indirect effect summed over every path through at least one mediator nie(x, type = "total")

Effects are for a unit change in the treatment. They have a causal reading only under the assumptions in Methods and Formulas; medfit computes the numbers, and the interpretation is yours.

The four-way decomposition

For one mediator and a treatment-by-mediator product, the total effect splits into four parts (page):

Term Meaning Formula
CDE controlled direct effect: the effect of the treatment with the mediator held at \(m^*\) \(\theta_1 + \theta_3 m^*\)
INTref reference interaction: interaction that would exist even if the treatment did not change the mediator \(\theta_3 \left( E[M \mid X = 0, \bar c] - m^* \right)\)
INTmed mediated interaction: interaction that depends on the treatment changing the mediator \(\theta_3 \beta_1\)
PIE pure indirect effect: mediation with no interaction \(\theta_2 \beta_1\)

They add up: TE = CDE + INTref + INTmed + PIE, NDE = CDE + INTref, and NIE = INTmed + PIE.

Term Meaning
m_star (\(m^*\)) the reference mediator level at which the CDE is evaluated (default 0)

Several mediators

Term Meaning Page
serial mediators in a chain: X to \(M_1\) to \(M_2\) to Y Serial mediation
parallel mediators side by side, with no path between them; NIE is \(\sum_j a_j b_j\) Parallel mediation
joint the joint natural effects of several mediators when the outcome has treatment-by-mediator products Joint mediation
skip path a path that jumps over a mediator in a chain, such as X to \(M_2\) Serial mediation

Clusters

Term Meaning
2-1-1 design treatment assigned to clusters; mediator and outcome measured on individuals
\(b_B\) (b_between) the effect of a cluster’s mean mediator on the outcome
\(b_W\) (b_within) the effect of an individual’s deviation from the cluster mean
own the part of the indirect effect that acts through a person’s own mediator
spillover the part that acts through the rest of the cluster
Kenward-Roger (se_type = "kr") a small-sample correction for mixed models that gives t intervals for the paths

See Cluster-randomized trials. The own and spillover split is a large-cluster approximation.

Inference

Term Meaning Page
delta method a standard error for a function of estimates (such as \(a b\)), from their covariance Which interval?
parametric bootstrap draws the paths from their estimated normal distribution Which interval?
nonparametric bootstrap resamples rows and refits Bootstrap Inference
plugin the point estimate only, with no interval Bootstrap Inference
percentile interval the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the bootstrap draws, for a 95% interval Bootstrap Inference
sandwich a robust standard error, used with weights (se_type = "sandwich"); HC3 for the glm engine, HC0-type for the native engine Weights and robust SEs
MBCO the minimum over the paths of the likelihood-ratio tests (two or k paths), for the hypothesis that an indirect effect is zero (mbco_sem()) constraints and MBCO

The native engine

Term Meaning Page
SEMFit the result of fit_sem(); extract_mediation() turns it into the classes above Native engine
label a name given to a path in syntax, as in y ~ b * m; equal labels are one parameter Native engine
defined parameter (:=) a quantity defined from labels, such as ab := a * b, with a delta-method standard error Native engine
latent variable (=~) a variable measured by indicators, as in eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3 a latent mediator
constraint an equality or inequality on labels, such as a == b constraints and MBCO
mean structure the observed means modeled together with the covariances: intercepts (y ~ 1) are estimated; any ~1 statement turns it on and frees every unwritten observed intercept Intercepts
intercept the mean of an observed variable that its equation leaves unexplained, written y ~ 1 or y ~ 1 + x; y ~ 0*1 fixes it at 0 and is a restriction Intercepts
fixed_x fixes the mean, variances and covariances of exogenous observed variables at their sample values, as lavaan’s fixed.x = TRUE; the structural estimates and standard errors do not change Fix exogenous covariates
product term x:m on the right side of a regression, an observed column equal to x * m; it gives the four-way decomposition and turns the mean structure on Product terms
dummy (group_mid) the 0/1 column a categorical covariate becomes in a native fit, one per non-reference level, named <column>_<level> Cookbook recipe 21
reference level the first level of a categorical covariate, which gets no dummy; the other levels are read against it Cookbook recipe 21
canonical name (m:x) the one name a product is stored under: the two variable names sorted in the C locale, so x:m and m:x are the same term Product terms
nested comparison (anova()) the likelihood-ratio test of a restricted fit against a fuller one; it refits nothing and refuses fits that are not nested Compare nested fits
conditional log likelihood the log likelihood given the fixed variables under fixed_x, so logLik(), AIC and BIC of fits with different fixed sets cannot be compared Limits
